--- title: "GFM Extensions" guide-section: "Core Concepts" tags: [Extensions, HTML, Tables] bread-crumbs: false --- This page explains the five GitHub Flavored Markdown extensions that multimark supports, with examples showing how each one works and how to combine them. ## What Are GFM Extensions? GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) extends the CommonMark specification with five additional syntax features. These are the constructs that GitHub recognizes in README files, issues, and pull requests but that are not part of the base CommonMark spec. Multimark supports all five GFM extensions through the `extensions` parameter, which accepts a sequence of extension names. Extensions are disabled by default so that the parser remains strictly CommonMark-compliant unless you opt in. ::: {#5b0943cd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import VALID_EXTENSIONS sorted(VALID_EXTENSIONS) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['autolink', 'strikethrough', 'table', 'tagfilter', 'tasklist'] ``` ::: ::: Each extension is independent: you enable only the ones you need. ## Tables The `table` extension adds pipe-table syntax. Columns are separated by `|` characters, and a header row is separated from body rows by a line of dashes. ::: {#7ec62208 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import markdown_to_html table_md = """\ | Feature | Status | |------------|--------| | Tables | ✓ | | Autolinks | ✓ | | Tasklists | ✓ | """ print(markdown_to_html(table_md, extensions=["table"])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```
Feature Status
Tables ✓
Autolinks ✓
Tasklists ✓
``` ::: ::: Column alignment is controlled with colons in the separator row: `:---` for left, `:---:` for center, and `---:` for right. The renderer emits `style="text-align: ..."` attributes on the `` and `` elements. ::: {#6d655856 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} aligned = """\ | Left | Center | Right | |:-----|:------:|------:| | a | b | c | """ print(markdown_to_html(aligned, extensions=["table"])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```
Left Center Right
a b c
``` ::: ::: ## Strikethrough The `strikethrough` extension recognizes `~~text~~` as deleted content, rendering it with `` tags. ::: {#f9d9bc11 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(markdown_to_html("This is ~~no longer~~ relevant.", extensions=["strikethrough"])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```

This is no longer relevant.

``` ::: ::: Strikethrough works inline alongside other formatting. You can combine it with bold, italic, and code spans without issue. ::: {#b3b968e6 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} combined = "~~**bold and struck**~~ and ~~`code struck`~~" print(markdown_to_html(combined, extensions=["strikethrough"])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```

bold and struck and code struck

``` ::: ::: ## Autolinks The `autolink` extension automatically converts bare URLs and email addresses into clickable links without requiring explicit Markdown link syntax. ::: {#0013b6ce .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} text = """\ Visit https://github.com for more info. Send feedback to user@example.com. """ print(markdown_to_html(text, extensions=["autolink"])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```

Visit https://github.com for more info.

Send feedback to user@example.com.

``` ::: ::: This is the same behavior you see on GitHub: any URL starting with `http://` or `https://` becomes a link, and email addresses get `mailto:` links. ## Tag Filtering The `tagfilter` extension suppresses a specific set of HTML tags that could be used for XSS attacks, even when `unsafe=True` is set.
